anchors: HMDFMBV3 (positive for Intersectional): the dataset pairs a combined group with its stereotype, such as ('Black+Women', 'Angry Black Woman'), section 2.3.

R7V99ERA (negative for enumerations): the introduction lists gender, disability and mental health status as dimensions studied elsewhere, while the work itself examines race, so only Race_Ethnicity is coded.
VSZM7CT6 (boundary): the sentence 'AI algorithms may reinforce racial and gender stereotypes' counts only when the work develops it as its own worked example.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Bias_Axes
analysis_field_definitions.note: Intersectional requires at least two axes treated in their interaction, not merely co-mentioned.
rules: An axis is coded when the work analyses bias along it, measures or compares groups along it, or uses it as a worked example in its own argument. An axis that appears only in an enumeration of protected attributes, in sample demographics, in a related-work passage or in an outlook is left uncoded.

Other_Axis is reserved for a social axis of disadvantage that the list lacks, such as caste or place of residence, and the axis is named in AN_Notes. Unspecified marginalised groups and non-social variables such as study subject or programming experience are no axes. Other_Axis never replaces a listed axis.
None applies when the work discusses bias without any axis it analyses in the sense of the first rule.

Race_Ethnicity covers racialisation and ethnic group, Nationality_Migration citizenship, country of origin and migration or refugee status, Language_Culture language, language variety and cultural region. The axis is coded under the name the work gives it, and both are coded when the work uses both.

Intersectional additionally requires a passage in which the outcome or argument depends on the combination of axes, such as a result for Black women that differs from the results for Black people and for women.

anchors: MS3CNU3S (taxonomy): Table 1 divides representational harms from allocational harms, the latter being the 'Disparate distribution of resources or opportunities between social groups'.
YMABYPKF (Indirect_Discrimination): an audit of names correlated with race and gender concludes that disparities 'may constitute bias in the form of disparate impact'.
7FEFMCBZ (allocational harm): a racial disparity in screen-in decisions of child welfare workers and an algorithm is discrimination, not only Disparate_Performance.
MA3LBJS6 (Exclusionary_Norms): digital first contact must not be the only route, since otherwise less digitally skilled help seekers are no longer reached.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Harm_Types
rules: A harm type is coded when the work demonstrates, measures or argues the mechanism for its own object, and every assigned value has its own passage. A harm named only in background, in a definitions table or in a related-work passage is left uncoded, and so is a harm the work only cites from other work, including a list of cited cases, when its own argument or result does not establish it. A review or taxonomy codes the harm types that structure its own synthesis as a section, table row or coded category.

Allocational harms are separated from representational harms first (Gallegos et al. 2024, Table 1). Direct_Discrimination and Indirect_Discrimination require an allocation or a decision about persons or groups, such as hiring, benefits, screening-in or a risk score. Output that depicts or describes a group is a representational harm.

Direct_Discrimination applies when the decision changes with the group attribute itself, stated in the input or the rule. Indirect_Discrimination applies when an apparently neutral criterion or proxy such as a name, postcode, prior service contact or digital access produces the disadvantage. An audit that varies names correlated with race or gender is indirect discrimination. When the work classifies the discrimination itself, its classification is coded.

Disparate_Performance covers differences in system quality between groups or language varieties, such as accuracy, error rate or recognition. A difference in decision outcomes is discrimination, a difference in quality is Disparate_Performance, and a work that shows both codes both. A difference in tone or style of model output between groups is not by itself Disparate_Performance.

Exclusionary_Norms applies when the norm of a dominant group acts as default and other groups are left out or devalued, such as a male default, cis-centric answers or the assumption of digitally skilled clients. Stereotyping ascribes attributes to a group, Erasure leaves a group or its experience out, Misrepresentation generalises an unrepresentative depiction to a group.

analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Population
analysis_field_definitions.note: Education_Professional restricted to professional or higher-education AI-literacy settings; general or unspecified context goes to Not_SW_Specific.

analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Task
analysis_field_definitions.note: Task of professional practice for which the work describes, tests or proposes the use of AI. Complements AN_Population, which records the field or group of addressees. Documentation_Recording and Administration are separated by the case reference. A general LLM benchmark without an application task receives None. A task outside social work, such as resume screening, receives Other_Task with the task named in AN_Notes.

anchors: GP4JDSI8 (Explicit): 'neither sex nor gender are essential, natural, or fixed properties'.
CYZQ6XPK (Implicit_Only): 'The gender biases we considered in this paper cover only binary gender.' in the limitations.
RAV6DAFQ (Not_Applicable): no passage treats gender as an object.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Gender_Definition
analysis_field_definitions.note: Whether the work says what it means by gender. Not_Applicable exactly when AN_Gender_Understanding is Not_Applicable, Absent exactly when it is Unclear. Sample demographics, a gender control variable or a single mention in an enumeration do not make gender an object. An Explicit code carries its defining passage with location.

anchors: AZJW38MF (Explicit): 'In social work it is common to define bias as a prejudice against certain problems'.
YMABYPKF (Explicit): bias is introduced through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Bias_Definition
analysis_field_definitions.note: Whether the work says what it means by bias. Explicit when the work determines bias, discrimination or unfairness in a sentence of its own or adopts a cited or technical determination explicitly, such as a fairness criterion or the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact. Implicit_Only when the understanding is recognisable from measurement or frame only. Absent when the work treats bias without either. Not_Applicable when bias is no object of the work. An Explicit code carries its defining passage with location.

anchors: 2EBHMYU4 (Social_Construct and Intersectional): 'the traditional understanding of gender as binary (male/female) is being challenged today' with intersectionality as frame.
3XMBE43Z (Non_Binary_Inclusive): 'we included variations that referenced non-binary individuals'.
22XEFRWP (boundary): 'Gender was dummy-coded (0 = woman, 1 = man)' is sample demography and decides nothing alone.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Gender_Understanding
analysis_field_definitions.note: The understanding of gender that underlies the work's own analysis. A conceptual statement that the analysis does not follow goes to AN_Notes and the value follows the analysis. Binary_Categorical and Non_Binary_Inclusive exclude each other. Unclear and Not_Applicable stand alone. Social_Construct and Intersectional combine with each other and with Non_Binary_Inclusive. Intersectional follows the rule of Intersectional in AN_Bias_Axes. Non_Binary_Inclusive needs genders beyond the binary as categories of the analysis, a limitation sentence does not suffice. Social_Construct needs an explicit statement in the work that gender is socially produced, a relation or a power structure.

anchors: 7L93JBLR (Yes): queer theory and intersectional feminism frame the treatment of gender equality in EU AI law.
CYZQ6XPK (No): an evaluation of gender bias without a theoretical frame.
analysis_field_definitions.name: AN_Theory_Reference
analysis_field_definitions.note: Yes when the work names a theory, theoretical tradition or theoretical concept and uses it to frame its treatment of gender or bias. A citation that supports an empirical finding is no theory reference, and a theory that frames neither gender nor bias does not count. Each theory is recorded as a source-linked theory reference with its passage and location, not as a closed code.

analysis.AN_Notes: Workshop report (Werkstattbericht) with three teaching scenarios in social work higher education. Prompting competence is treated as learning content, a declared prompting appendix and Chain-of-Thought prompting are recommended; Role_Persona rests on the role play in which ChatGPT simulates a help-seeking person. Bias is named generically (normierendes und diskriminierendes Potenzial) without an axis or a harm mechanism for the work's own object. The 'Verzerrungen' in the role play scenario concern realism of the simulated client, not social bias. Mitigation is the proposed curricular embedding of the discriminatory potential in teaching. Rammert's technology theory frames AI as an actor, not gender or bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Pre-post evaluation of a 7-hour AI literacy course on machine learning concepts with university students in Hong Kong; research question 3 asks whether the course narrows gaps between genders and study backgrounds. Bias_Axes Gender because female and male participants are compared on concepts test, literacy and empowerment (Sections 4.1, 4.4, Table 5); study background and programming experience are non-social variables and not coded. Harm_Types None: the work establishes no harm mechanism of an AI system; gender stereotypes are cited to explain the empowerment gap. Mitigation: the course is an identifiable training intervention whose reported result is that the pre-course gender gap in self-perceived AI empowerment no longer existed after the course (Table 5); it addresses a gender gap in AI learning, not algorithmic bias, so Organisational_Process and Evaluated are limited to this training and its own pre-post result. AN_Task None: AI is the learning content, the work describes no professional task performed with AI. Gender is used as two categories (both genders) without definition. Theory_Reference No: self-efficacy (Bandura) and programming empowerment frame empowerment, not gender or bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Experiments on the emotional content of responses of seven LLMs to heteronormative versus non-heteronormative prompts and to LGBTQ+ slang. Axes: queer identity expressed through language (Sexual_Orientation_Identity) and queer slang as a language variety, 'minority slangs and argots' (Language_Culture). The more negative emotion labels for queer slang are a difference in tone and are therefore not coded as Disparate_Performance; Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own result and argument that guardrails against heteronormative language leave a bias against queer language. Bias definition: the adopted Vasquez definition determines heteronormative language as the input category of the experiments; LLM bias itself is recognisable only from the measurement of disproportionately negative emotional labels, so Implicit_Only. Existing safety guardrails are inferred from response patterns and are not an identified or assessed mitigation, so mitigation is None. Gender understanding: the heteronormativity frame treats traditional gender roles, binary gender norms and cisnormativity as normative orders encoded in language, which is taken as the explicit statement for Social_Construct; this is a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1 and is flagged. Theory reference: the heteronormativity taxonomy of Marchia and Sommer with the definition of Vasquez et al. ICL: GPT-4o tagging prompt with definition and three annotated examples.

analysis.AN_Notes: Narrative review that builds the five-component framework Reflexive Prompt Engineering (Section 1.2). General_Guidance: 'prompts can be intentionally crafted or augmented with instructions to avoid bias' (3.1.3). ICL: balanced, randomly ordered few-shot examples, debiasing and counterfactual attribute flipping (3.1.1). Thought_Generation: chain-of-thought with ethical checkpoints (3.1.2). Self_Criticism: separate verification step 'Plan verification questions to fact-check this draft' (3.1.2). Object_of_Critique: chain-of-thought explanations as an 'illusion of transparency' (3.1.2). Learning_Content: the work positions responsible prompt engineering as a core competency of AI literacy and names its incorporation into curricula and training programmes (Abstract, Section 2.2, Section 4). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender and race appear only as attributes to flip and in a cited replacement example, not as an axis the work analyses. AN_Harm_Types None: stereotyping, toxicity and the Gemini misrepresentation incident are cited from other sources or named as tool targets, the framework establishes no harm mechanism of its own. Mitigation Proposed: debiasing through prompt design, documentation, stakeholder involvement and human oversight are recommended without an own or synthesised assessment. AN_Task None: recruitment, performance reviews and legal analysis illustrate a general framework. AN_Theory_Reference No: value-sensitive design is named as an aligned responsibility-by-design approach and frames neither gender nor bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Formal hypercube framework for intersectional fairness with proofs, a variance-based metric family (VarRatio) and verification on synthetic data and the Adult dataset. Studientyp Konzept: the core contribution is the framework, the propagation algorithm and the metrics; the synthetic and real-data experiments serve to verify the theoretical results. Gender, ethnicity and age are the work's own worked examples and the Adult protected attributes (marital status is a further attribute, not coded as a social axis of disadvantage). Indirect_Discrimination: the work defines worst case disparate impact and statistical parity for the outcomes of a binary classification, proves their propagation and finds intersectional bias in Adult; the classification follows the work's own use of disparate impact. Disparate_Performance: section 4.2 and Appendix B extend the framework to Equality of Opportunity, 'that seek to equalize the performance of our model on different subgroups', and prove that worst case accuracy, precision and error-rate disparities narrow up the levels; this rests on the work's own derivation and is not measured empirically. Gender is binary by construction (binary protected attributes, male/female). No mitigation is applied; bottom-up fairness is a design principle without a stage. Theory reference: Crenshaw's intersectionality from Black feminist scholarship frames the problem.

analysis.AN_Notes: Philosophische Analyse der Paritaetsdeutung intersektionaler Fairness. Sexual_Orientation_Identity aus dem eigenen Argument zu nicht-binaeren und trans Personen im Koerperscanner und zu nicht-heterosexuellen Paaren bei Hypothekenvergabe. Schadensarten aus dem eigenen Argument: Gesichtserkennung mit hoechster Fehlerrate fuer Schwarze Frauen (Disparate_Performance, Ursachenanalyse in 3.1), strukturelle Cisnormativitaet (Exclusionary_Norms), fehlende Kategorie nonbinary im Algorithmus (Erasure), hypothetischer Einstellungsalgorithmus, der weisse Maenner gegenueber asiatischen Frauen bevorzugt (Direct_Discrimination; das Werk klassifiziert die Diskriminierung nicht selbst als unmittelbar oder mittelbar, die Zuordnung folgt daraus, dass die Entscheidung an Rasse und Geschlecht haengt). Massnahme: Abkehr von reiner Paritaet hin zu starker Fairness mit gemeinschaftsbasierter, interdisziplinaerer Entwicklung (Organisational_Process, Proposed); Kearns u. a. werden kritisiert, nicht vorgeschlagen. Other_Task: Rueckfallprognose, Personalauswahl, Hochschulzulassung, Kreditvergabe, Gesichtserkennung und Sicherheitsscanner. Theorien: Intersektionalitaet (Crenshaw, Collins), strukturelle Unterdrueckung und nicht-distributive Gerechtigkeit (Young), intersectional critical race technology studies.

analysis.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI in social sciences and social work 2022 to 2025. The synthesis has its own section 'Algorithmic Discrimination and Bias' and case-study section; axes coded from these: race (COMPAS) and low income (child-welfare flagging, Robodebt). Disability and single mothers appear in one sentence on French welfare litigation only. Indirect_Discrimination: allocation decisions (child-welfare flagging, debt notices, risk scores) that disadvantage groups through historical training data and data matching, without the group attribute as decision criterion; the work does not itself classify direct or indirect. Mitigation: diverse training datasets (Pre_Processing), adversarial debiasing and fairness constraints (In_Training), human oversight, bias audits and collaborative governance (Organisational_Process); the review reports these as implemented in pilot programmes without a reported result, hence Demonstrated. Source-quality note: several references carry placeholder URLs ('xxxx') and implausible bibliographic data, flagged for the domain experts; codes rely only on the work's own statements. AI Agent Review: Health_Care is kept because section 3.3 addresses health monitoring, telemedicine and virtual nursing in disability and elderly care as a field of the review.

analysis.AN_Notes: Critical survey and typology of feminist AI (model, design, policy, discourse, culture, science). Bias axes gender and race carry the work's own argument on technoliberal inclusion and racial capitalism; class and LGBTQI+ appear in enumerations. Intersectional left uncoded: intersectionality is named as a strand of feminism, the combination examples (facial recognition, Sinders data set) are reported from other work. AN_Harm_Types None: 'male as norm', stereotyped word embeddings and gender-bias norms are reported positions of cited authors, the typology is not structured by harm types. Mitigation: Sinders' bias-correcting data collection (Pre_Processing) and participatory design in Poieto (Organisational_Process) are reported as applied in small projects without evaluation, hence Demonstrated, a synthesised status. Social_Construct rests on the adopted feminist STS frame and Wajcman's 'historical and cultural construction of gender'; gender is not defined in an own sentence. AI Agent Review: AN_Task None, because the work types conceptions of feminist AI; the legal knowledge prototype, the court transparency system and the Mumkin chatbot are reported projects illustrating the typology, not a task of professional practice for which the work itself describes or proposes AI use.

Gender definition adopted from Butler's relational understanding within the theoretical framework, which also carries Social_Construct.

analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual, literature-based paper on AI (machine learning, intelligent tutoring, teacherbots, VR simulation, AI grading) in higher education and its implications for social work education. Bias_Axes None: 'AI algorithms may reinforce racial and gender stereotypes' is cited from Howard and Borenstein (2017) and not developed as the work's own example (codebook boundary anchor VSZM7CT6, a record of this work). Harm_Types None: developer bias in child-protection predictive risk modelling and the beneficence problem are reported from cited work, not established by the work's own argument. Mitigation None: the proposed critical digital literacies address AI understanding in social work education generally and are not presented as a measure against bias. AN_Task Teaching_Further_Education for AI in teaching, assessment, tutoring and simulation in social work education. Gender is no object; 'gender stereotypes' appears once in a cited sentence. Bias is understood as structural inequity built into human-made systems without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only. Theory_Reference Yes: Braidotti's critical posthumanism, whose 'Convergence' of speedy transformations and persistent inequalities directly precedes and frames the work's statement on bias and structural inequity, and frames its questions of power; the line between a framing concept and an illustrative mention is a recorded open question of the codebook. Feministisch stays nein because Braidotti is used as posthuman theory without a gender-related power analysis.

analysis.AN_Notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); the baselines comprise 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. Evaluated: CCSV outperforms all baselines on automated and human evaluation (Sections 5.1, 6). Fine-tuning with CCSV data is named only as future work and not coded as In_Training. Language_Culture through the culture-diversity task rated by humans (Section 6.2). Erasure: under-representation or erasure of demographic groups in the responses, measured as entropy close to 0. Exclusionary_Norms: the work's own baseline output defaults to 'only white male CEOs' when the prompt is under-specified, which the work attributes to implicit assumptions of the model (Abstract, Section 1). AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical with Implicit_Only: the analysis uses fixed knowledge-graph labels male, female and other, and the work itself states that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female and that the gender signal is incomplete (footnote 2, Limitations), so no gender beyond the binary is a category of the analysis; boundary case for the domain experts. Identity: corpus and text titles differ in wording, see identity_check. AN_Task None: general LLM evaluation without a professional task.

analysis.AN_Notes: Critical commentary proposing two feminist ChatGPT assignments for a university economics classroom. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Students could enter such a prompt, or experiment with rephrased prompts as in Figure 2, then critically examine ChatGPT's generated paragraphs'. The bias the work itself treats is epistemic, definitions biased toward mainstream economic thinking and reproduced knowledge hierarchies; gender bias in generative models and patriarchal value systems are only cited (Bolukbasi et al. 2016, Prabhakaran et al. 2022), and race, class and gender appear only as social locations in a reflection task, so no bias axis, no harm type and no Gender category are coded. Mitigation: the critical-citation assignment as an educational measure, proposed. Feminist epistemology and standpoint theory frame the treatment of bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

analysis.AN_Notes: Theoretische Analyse mit Literaturreview, Hauptbeitrag ist ein rechtebasiertes Rahmenwerk aus vier Komponenten (ethische AI Literacy, partizipative Governance, kontinuierliche Folgenabschätzung, gemeinwesenorientierte Advocacy) mit Empfehlungen in Tabelle 1, daher Studientyp Konzept. Generative KI wird nicht behandelt. AN_Bias_Axes Socioeconomic und AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination aus dem im eigenen Argument zu Groupthink ausgeführten Fall eines Risikoinstruments der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, das armutsbezogene Faktoren als Missbrauchsindikatoren wertete. Grenzfall, weil der Fall aus der Literatur übernommen ist. Erasure aus dem eigenen Argument zur epistemischen Ungerechtigkeit, nach dem Algorithmen das Erfahrungswissen marginalisierter Gemeinschaften diskontieren. Rassismus erscheint nur in einer Policy-Empfehlung und in Fallnennungen, nicht als analysierte Achse. Alle Maßnahmen sind organisatorisch und vorgeschlagen (Schulung, Supervision, Beteiligung, Audit, Monitoring), das empirische Testen des Rahmenwerks steht in den Limitationen als offene Aufgabe. Bias wird über strukturelle Ungleichheit und differenzielle Wirkungen gerahmt, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über epistemische Ungerechtigkeit nach Fricker, TAM, I-C-E-Modell und sozioökologische Systemtheorie rahmen Technikakzeptanz und Implementierung, nicht Bias. Geschlecht wird nicht behandelt.

analysis.AN_Notes: Prompt audit of GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and GPT-4o with regular and flipped Likert-scale prompts on willingness to rent to, work with, marry into the family of, live next to or entrust children to American or North Korean persons with six mental-disability conditions (bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, remitted and symptomatic), plus requested explanations. Mental disability is coded as Disability, the axis the work names; the intersection is nationality with mental disability, without gender. The scenarios elicit attitudes, not decisions about persons, so no discrimination type is coded and the harms are representational. Bias is measured as rating differences and the authors call its interpretation subjective, hence Implicit_Only. The intersectional lens combines nationality and mental disability without a power or gender analysis, so Feministisch stays nein. The mitigation is a future-work recommendation to represent a spectrum of mental disability symptoms in training data. No social work setting.

analysis.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual and intersectional analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (privilege and discrimination, ideology, everyday scenarios) on micro, meso and macro levels, complemented by a review of online and academic sources. Prompts serve as research instrument; minimal prompts simulate everyday internet users without prompt-engineering knowledge. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: users 'being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use, and what kind of aesthetics they pick into the images'. AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs of the tool for everyday users and tests no professional application task; creative and design practice of artists appears as context and addressee of recommendations in the discussion. Axes from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability, body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine and Global North default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and the Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). The confederate-flag finding concerns imagery, not language, so Toxicity is not coded. Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Gender definition from footnote 2, which defines the binary gender norm and replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations; it is a terminological determination rather than a definition of gender in the narrow sense.

AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs of the tool for everyday users and tests no professional application task; creative and design practice of artists appears as context and addressee of recommendations in the discussion. Axes from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability, body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine and Global North default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and the Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Gender definition from footnote 2, which defines the binary gender norm and replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations; it is a terminological determination rather than a definition of gender in the narrow sense.

analysis.AN_Notes: Interdisziplinäre rechtlich-technische Analyse, die Fairnessmaße und Verfahren der Bias-Minderung mit EU-Recht und AI Act kontrastiert und individuelle Fairness als rechtlich passenderes Konzept begründet, keine eigene Datenerhebung. Studientyp Theoretisch, weil das Werk ohne Suchmethode referiert und argumentativ schließt. AN_Bias_Axes Gender und Race_Ethnicity aus eigenen Arbeitsbeispielen (Datenaugmentation durch Geschlechtertausch, Kreditvergabe an zwei ethnische Gruppen), Intersectional aus dem Abschnitt zu Gruppen an der Schnittstelle zweier Achsen und der eigenen Kritik, dass das EU-Recht Diskriminierungsgründe nur einzeln betrachtet. Socioeconomic bleibt uncodiert, wirtschaftlicher oder sozialer Status steht nur als Aufzählung. AN_Harm_Types Direct_Discrimination und Indirect_Discrimination, weil das Werk Diskriminierung selbst als unmittelbar und mittelbar einschließlich Proxy-Diskriminierung klassifiziert. Disparate_Performance nicht codiert, die Fehlerratenvergleiche sind Fairnesskriterien und der einzige Qualitätsunterschied zwischen Gruppen ist das zitierte Ergebnis von Buolamwini und Gebru. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated gilt nur für das synthetisierte Ergebnis von Tyagi et al. (erweiterter Variational Autoencoder mindert Gender-Bias statischer Worteinbettungen), alle übrigen Verfahren und die Empfehlungen zu Audits, Dokumentation und interdisziplinären Teams sind Inventar oder Vorschlag. Geschlecht erscheint nur binär in Beispielen, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über prozedurale Fairness nach Tyler, die rechtliche Unterscheidung unmittelbarer und mittelbarer Diskriminierung und individuelle Fairness nach Dwork et al.

analysis.AN_Notes: Philosophischer Beitrag: AI bias als strukturelle Ungerechtigkeit nach Iris Marion Young, Fallbeispiel Gesundheitsversorgung entlang von vier Entwicklungsstufen. Bias-Achsen aus der eigenen Stufenanalyse: race (Hautkrebsdaten, Kostenproxy, VBAC), gender (gender research gap) und class oder Einkommen (10/90 gap, EHR-Verfügbarkeit, Versicherung). Schadensarten aus der eigenen Stufenanalyse in Abschnitt 3.2, die zitierte Fälle als Belege des eigenen Arguments ausführt: Disparate_Performance (schiefe Daten, bessere Leistung für hellhäutige Personen), Direct_Discrimination (Race als Input des VBAC-Scores), Indirect_Discrimination (Gesundheitskosten als Proxy für Bedarf, ZIP-Code). Die Anerkennungs- und Repräsentationsbeispiele in 4.1 (Menstruations-App nach Eveleth, Suchmaschine nach Noble) illustrieren nur die begriffliche Erweiterung über Ressourcenverteilung hinaus und bleiben nach Codebuch 1.4.1 als zitierte Fälle uncodiert. Evaluated beschränkt sich auf die synthetisierte Studie von Pierson et al. (2021): patientenberichtete Schmerzwerte als Label und diverser Datensatz (Pre_Processing) senken unerklärte Schmerzdisparitäten; keine eigene Evaluation. Übrige Empfehlungen (Table 1, Minipublics, Beteiligung Marginalisierter, Monitoring) bleiben Vorschläge. AN_Task Other_Task: klinische Diagnose und Bedarfsschätzung in der Medizin. Gender als teilweiser Gegenstand ohne bestimmbares Verständnis, daher Absent und Unclear.

analysis.AN_Notes: Three studies with ChatGPT 3.5 and 4o: cultural value scales (Study 1), 13 one-round decision tasks with country personas and country interactants (Study 2), four prompt strategies as intervention (Study 3). Role_Persona: 'If you are an ordinary individual from [the country]' as instrument; General_Guidance covers the debiasing cues 'From a fairness perspective,', 'As an independent individual, please make a choice according to your own ideas and', 'If you live in a future world.' and 'Imagine you live in a multicultural world,'. Evaluated: the prompt strategies reduced country differences to non-significance in most tested task-model combinations, but the personal-preference prompt failed in the GPT-4o public goods game (own experiment). Axes coded as the work names them, countries/nationality and cultural groups. Direct_Discrimination: allocation decisions (dictator, ultimatum, public goods) toward interactants vary with the nationality stated in the prompt; these are simulated game allocations, not real decisions about persons. Training-data and oversight recommendations in the discussion are outlook and not coded as stages. Theory: Hofstede's cultural dimensions and GLOBE dimensions frame the explanation of the bias sources. Gender appears only as the GLOBE dimension gender egalitarianism, not as an object. Review: Diversitaet teilweise, weil das Werk die Wahrnehmung von Personen aus 20 Laendern und einen respektvollen interkulturellen Umgang als nachgeordneten Teilaspekt behandelt. Direct_Discrimination beruht auf simulierten Zuteilungen im Spiel und bleibt ein Grenzfall fuer die Fachpruefung.

analysis.AN_Notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument, and the three context levels test prompt design. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric information in the prompt), which the work's own experiment shows to remove name-based disparities in most scenarios, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); routine audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names, although the authors state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm type: Indirect_Discrimination following the codebook anchor, since names act as proxies in numeric advice about persons (offers, salaries, chances) and the work interprets the disparities as disparate impact. The outputs are allocative decisions, not depictions of groups, and the encoded stereotypes are the authors' explanation of the mechanism; Stereotyping is therefore not coded as a separate representational harm. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference, a boundary case between legal doctrine and theory).

analysis.AN_Notes: Debiasing framework for text-to-image generation in which a fine-tuned LLM rewrites generic prompts to match target demographic distributions; evaluated against ground-truth ratios and regex and NER baselines. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'transform generic prompts devoid of demographic specifics into those that are demographically informed'. ICL: few-shot prompting of GPT-3 for training data. Mitigation stages: Prompt_Practice for the rewriting of prompts before a frozen image model, and In_Training for the proportional fine-tuning of the rewriting LLM with learning rates scaled by the measured bias per demographic characteristic (section 3.2.4, Algorithms 2 and 3). The work classifies its method as post-processing, but it changes no output of the image model, so Post_Processing is not coded. Status Evaluated: the reduction of the gap between generated and target ratios for ethnicity and gender is reported. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own observation that generic prompts default to White subjects and prioritise certain groups. Gender is analysed as male and female; the limitation sentence that gender should not be confined to the binary does not change the analysis.

analysis.AN_Notes: Short conceptual risk analysis of ChatGPT and AI in social work (data security, algorithmic bias, ethics, legal risks) with countermeasures. Bias_Axes Socioeconomic: economically disadvantaged groups are the work's own example of data imbalance in social services; 'minority groups' and 'marginalized groups' stay unspecified and are not coded. Harm_Types from the work's own risk argument: Disparate_Performance (inadequate data on underrepresented groups hinders systems from accurately gauging their needs) and Direct_Discrimination (feedback-loop bias leading to denial of services and resources 'based on their inherent characteristics'); the work does not itself separate direct from indirect discrimination, and the phrase is read as a decision changing with the group attribute. The single sentence that biases threaten to perpetuate stereotypes is asserted without mechanism and not coded as Stereotyping. Mitigation proposed: diverse and representative datasets (Pre_Processing); transparency, explainability, oversight, training of social workers and legal regulation (Organisational_Process). Training ChatGPT to warn on sensitive topics concerns illicit content, not bias, and is not coded as In_Training. AN_Task Case_Assessment_Decision_Support for risk assessment algorithms and AI-driven decisions about services. Bias is explained through data imbalance and feedback loops without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only.

analysis.AN_Notes: Practice guide for managers and staff in small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS prompting framework, organisational measures and own image-prompt trials in DALL-E 2 and Midjourney. Publication type admitted as scholarly grey literature (university publisher, named authorship, source list, expert contributions), flagged for the domain experts. Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and company images in HR and marketing. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'Es könnte z.B. explizit gefordert werden, dass Frauen und Männer, Menschen unterschiedlicher Hautfarbe und sozialer Schicht dargestellt werden sollen.' Further strategies: choose the context deliberately, prompt in English ('female and male bosses'), weigh neutrality against explicit diversity, omit gender in recommendation letters or use a 'Verwirrungstaktik', anonymise. Bias axes and harm types rest on the guide's own image-prompt observations and its own job-advertisement argument (Indirect_Discrimination: job-advertisement language that appeals to men deters women and is perpetuated by training); cited news cases are not used. Mitigation status Evaluated applies only to adding 'divers' to the prompt, whose effect is tested in two tools and reported as small; the trial is informal (one prompt), and the other measures (data diversity, targeted training with gender-inclusive terms, governance, training of staff, monitoring, human review) are proposed. Gender understanding: the image analysis contrasts women and men, so Binary_Categorical follows the analysis; the Gender Data Gap remark on genderqueer people, the gender star and 'alle Gender' are conceptual statements that the analysis does not follow. Intersectional rests on the guide's own statement that women and especially Women of Color are sexualised in generated images. Theory reference No: 'Feministische KI' appears only in the outlook as a positive narrative with the MissJourney example, and Data Feminism and the Gender Data Gap appear as further reading or illustration; none of them frames the guide's treatment of gender or bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Experiment mit fünf LLMs auf StereoSet und GenAssocBias, Messgröße ist die Rate stereotyper Antworten, ergänzt um sechs Debiasing-Prompts. General_Guidance steht für die System-2-Anweisung 'You answer questions slowly and thoughtfully.' und die Debiasing-Anweisung 'The response should be unbiased and does not rely on stereotypes', Thought_Generation für 'Let's think step-by-step', Role_Persona für 'Adopt the identity of a person/machine'. Evaluiert wird die eigene Prompt-Intervention, HP Debias schneidet im Mittel am besten ab, CoT erhöht stereotype Antworten in jedem Minimalpaar. Bias-Achsen nach den gemessenen Kategorien, Beauty als Physical_Appearance. Profession, beauty in profession und institutional bleiben als nicht-soziale Variablen uncodiert. Gender ist eine von neun Messkategorien ohne Bestimmung des Begriffs. Theoriebezug ist die Dual-Process-Theorie, die die Entstehung sozialer Bias im Modell rahmt.

analysis.AN_Notes: Ethische Erörterung ohne eigene Daten, gestützt auf den NASW-Code und die Technologiestandards. Algorithmischer Bias ist eines von neun ethischen Themen. Race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation und gender expression stehen nur in Aufzählungen geschützter Kategorien, daher AN_Bias_Axes None. AN_Harm_Types: nicht entscheidbar aus Fulltext. Das Werk argumentiert in eigenen Worten eine verzerrte Beurteilung von Klient:innen durch nicht repräsentative Trainingsdaten, also eine Entscheidung über Personen, ordnet sie aber weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung ein und nennt kein Kriterium und kein stellvertretendes Merkmal. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind die Datenbehandlung zur Bias-Reduktion (Pre_Processing) sowie Ethik-Steuerungskomitee, diverse Fokusgruppen, Peer Review von Algorithmen, Simulationen, Schulung und Testprotokoll (Organisational_Process). AN_Task folgt den im Werk beschriebenen Einsätzen, nämlich KI-gestützte Beurteilung und Diagnostik, Kommunikation mit Klient:innen über KI, ChatGPT für Förderanträge und Fundraising sowie der KI-gestützte Crisis Contact Simulator zur Schulung von Beratenden. Bias wird über nicht repräsentative Daten und Ungleichbehandlung geschützter Gruppen erkennbar, aber nicht bestimmt. Die Ethikstandards sind kein Theoriebezug.

analysis.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. analysis.AN_Notes: Research agenda for a feminist metaethics of AI; object is AI ethics as a field, AI in general. Mitigation: proposed research into the diversity of AI ethics boards and the inclusion of those hitherto ignored in decision-making (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, class, race, disability and sexuality appear only as a programmatic enumeration and outlook, cited case studies are suggestions, no bias is analysed. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional rests on the work's own argument that AI impact is to be examined depending on gender in interaction with other identity markers; boundary case, since the argument is programmatic and no definition of gender is given (Implicit_Only from the intersectional feminist frame). Bias as structural domination and oppression is recognisable from the frame only. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Axes stays None because the work analyses no bias along any axis; gender with class, race, disability and sexuality appears as a programmatic research direction of the agenda (Section 3.4) and cited AI cases are illustrative case studies. Prompts are the research instrument; sentence-completion and story prompts carry no codable technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from Study 1 (gender and career or family, age and pleasantness), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from Study 2 (subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North and South). Intersectional because Study 3 reports occupations that depend on the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard), although the work lists the need for intersectional analysis as a limitation. Harm_Types from own results: Stereotyping (gendered role associations, stereotyped occupations and story themes) and Derogatory_Language (sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions). Mitigation recommendations only: diverse and inclusive training data and data augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF guidelines (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments, diverse teams, stakeholder participation and literacy initiatives (Organisational_Process). analysis.AN_Notes: Das Werk entwirft KI-bezogene Kompetenzdimensionen (kognitiv, affektiv, handlungsbezogen) und eine eigene Übersicht der Besonderheiten algorithmen-basierter Diskriminierung (Tab. 1) für die Medienpädagogik. Nationality_Migration und Language_Culture stützen sich auf die berichtete Fokusgruppenstudie der Autorinnen mit Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte (Klassifizierung nach kultureller Zugehörigkeit, Zuordnung zu einem Mehrheitssprachensystem, Autokorrektur ausländisch klingender Namen). Age stützt sich auf das ausgeführte Proxy-Beispiel im Bewerbungsverfahren. Geschlecht, Einkommen, Bildung und Religion stehen nur in Aufzählungen. Intersektionalität wird als Merkmal benannt, aber ohne Ergebnis oder Argument, das von einer Kombination abhängt, daher kein Intersectional. Indirect_Discrimination folgt aus der eigenen Übersicht (Proxy-Variablen) und dem Bewerbungsbeispiel, Exclusionary_Norms aus der Mehrheitssprach-Norm in der eigenen Studie. Die von Schober et al. berichteten beleidigenden Inhalte sind zitiert und nicht codiert. Maßnahmen sind vorgeschlagen, nämlich medienpädagogische Kompetenzförderung, Austauschforen, Meldesysteme, Beratungsstrukturen und regulatorische Anpassung des AGG. Kein theoretischer Rahmen für Bias, die Kompetenzdimensionen rahmen Kompetenz, nicht Bias. Studientyp Konzept, weil das Werk ein eigenes Modell der Kompetenzdimensionen (Abb. 1) und eine eigene Übersicht der Besonderheiten algorithmenbasierter Diskriminierung mit zugeordneten Kompetenzen (Tab. 1) entwirft und daraus Handlungsstrategien für die Medienpädagogik ableitet. Intersektionale Diskriminierung wird in einem Satz und einer Tabellenzeile benannt, ohne eigene Machtanalyse, daher Feministisch nein.

analysis.AN_Notes: Case-study based argument for a technical-critical social work pedagogy on ADM (AFST, COMPAS, NDIS, HEALER, Heat List). Bias axes follow the authors' own case analyses: disability in AFST child-protection screening and NDIS eligibility, racialised over-policing in the Heat List teaching case, socio-economic standing in AFST rent and school-attendance data and in the conclusion; COMPAS race disparity is cited only. Indirect_Discrimination: NDIS template scores used for eligibility and resource allocation overlook the individual impact of disability, and the proximity-based Heat List score leads to over-policing of African-American communities. Mitigation: critical case-study pedagogy with guiding questions on built-in social biases, applied in the authors' own undergraduate teaching without reported evaluation (Demonstrated), plus retained human interpretative screening. Feministisch teilweise rests on intersectional analysis of power used as a pedagogical frame without a gender perspective. Gender appears only in an enumeration (misogyny). AI Agent Review: Studientyp Konzept because the second part designs a case-study pedagogy with a five-question interrogation scheme; Demonstrated because the authors report using the method in their own undergraduate teaching with student conclusions on HEALER and no reported evaluation result.

analysis.AN_Notes: General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Writing clear and detailed prompts to generate relevant and personalised content for youth.' and 'Training youth workers to divide information clearly and into defined blocks - prompts - will make it easier for AI systems to understand and process their input.' (4.2.4.4 National Focus Group - Portugal, Q4 and Q5). Prompting is a competence to be trained (Learning_Content) and a recommended practice. AN_Population: the codebook has no value for general youth work. The report addresses youth work professionals in non-formal education without any focus on homelessness or precarious living conditions, so Homelessness_Youth is not supported; youth work is coded as part of child and youth services (Child_Family_Welfare) together with Education_Professional for the professional AI-literacy setting (resolved by the AI Agent Review, vocabulary gap flagged for domain experts). Bias axis: only the language barrier from the work's own focus groups (AI tools primarily in English, Greek-speaking youth and youth workers disadvantaged, 4.2.4.3 Q3 and 4.2.5) is coded as Language_Culture; gender and age differences come from a reported survey (3.2) without a bias analysis and are not coded as axes. Harm: English as default language of AI tools limits usability for non-English-speaking youth workers and young people (Exclusionary_Norms, own focus-group result, boundary case). Mitigation: training and critical evaluation of AI output to avoid biases are proposed as competences of youth workers, no evaluation. Gender understanding follows the male/female comparison of section 3.2, taken up in the conclusions, without a definition (Implicit_Only, Binary_Categorical). Bias understanding is recognisable only as bias inherited from training data (Implicit_Only). Competence frameworks (DigComp, ETS model, Hofstede's dimensions) frame neither gender nor bias, so no theory reference. Studientyp Empirisch because the focus groups with youth work professionals are the work's own data; the report also contains a desk review of competence frameworks.

The report addresses youth work professionals in non-formal education without any focus on homelessness or precarious living conditions, so Homelessness_Youth is not supported; youth work is coded as part of child and youth services (Child_Family_Welfare) together with Education_Professional for the professional AI-literacy setting (resolved by the AI Agent Review, vocabulary gap flagged for domain experts). Gender understanding follows the male/female comparison of section 3.2, taken up in the conclusions, without a definition (Implicit_Only, Binary_Categorical). Competence frameworks (DigComp, ETS model, Hofstede's dimensions) frame neither gender nor bias, so no theory reference. Studientyp Empirisch because the focus groups with youth work professionals are the work's own data; the report also contains a desk review of competence frameworks.

analysis.AN_Notes: Survey ('on the horizon' article) of data selection bias and an inventory of eleven social bias types, each with own completions from GPT-2, GPT-3 and BLOOM and Machine Translation examples from Google Translate and DeepL. Prompting role Research_Instrument because the inventory examples are elicited through text-completion inputs. The sentence on prompt templates as a source of selection bias is a single statement and was not coded as Object_of_Critique. Bias axes are the inventory sections 3.1 to 3.11 and section 2.4, each with own worked examples. Intersectional from the argument that bias against Black women can exist without overall race or gender bias. Harm types from own examples and own argument: stereotyping across the inventory, derogatory output ('he is inferior to white people'), better performance for high-resource languages, values of a dominant culture through English-centric data. Discrimination in COMPAS, hiring and healthcare is cited from other work and stays uncoded. Mitigation: data balancing, gender swapping and corpus selection (Pre_Processing), domain adaptation and bias avoidance when training (In_Training), all as directions. AN_Gender_Understanding: the gender section works with he and she, non-binary people appear only in a cited sentence and in one completion under sexual orientation, the pairing with Intersectional follows section 3.11 and is an open rule question. Theory reference intersectionality frames section 3.11. AI Agent Review: Diversitaet ja because the representation of demographic groups, languages and cultures in training corpora carries the data-selection half of the article (sections 2.3 and 2.4) and returns in the conclusion as increasing diversity. Feministisch teilweise because section 3.11 adopts intersectionality as an explicit, subordinate analytic frame.

analysis.AN_Notes: Vorschlag eines EPAS-Kompetenzindikators mit vier Fertigkeiten für das MSW-Curriculum. Prompting ist Lerninhalt (Fertigkeit 2) und empfohlene Praxis. Thought_Generation (Chain of Thought) und Role_Persona (Personas aus dem Prompt-Pattern-Katalog nach White et al.) sind als zu vermittelnde Techniken genannt. General_Guidance steht für das iterative Vorgehen 'The tasks of prompting and validating are often iterative'. Bias-Achsen und Schadensbeispiele (Bias gegenüber Frauen, People of Color, sexuell und geschlechtlich minorisierten Personen, CEO-Bilder, race-based medicine) sind zitierte Befunde anderer Arbeiten und nicht als eigene Analyse codiert, Geschlecht ist daher kein Gegenstand. Organisational_Process ist die vorgeschlagene Ausbildungsmaßnahme, Studierende sollen Ausgaben auf Bias prüfen und Minderung diskutieren. AN_Task folgt den im Werk beschriebenen Einsätzen, nämlich Behandlungspläne und Fallnotizen (Documentation_Recording), Materialien für Einzel- und Gruppensitzungen und Übersetzungen (Counselling_Client_Communication), Förderanträge und Fundraising (Administration), Schulungsmaterialien für die Fortbildung (Teaching_Further_Education) sowie die Zusammenfassung von Policy-Dokumenten und Entwürfe von Advocacy-Material auf Makroebene (Other_Task, Policy-Analyse und Advocacy). Bias wird nur als Spiegel der Trainingsdaten erkennbar.

analysis.AN_Notes: Konzeptionelles Policy-Paper der Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, das Feminist AI als Rahmen vorschlägt. Bias-Achse Geschlecht als eigenes Argument (männlich dominierte Verzerrungen, binäre Geschlechterkategorien schließen nicht-binäre Personen aus). Ethnizität, Klasse, Alter und weitere Kategorien stehen nur in der Bestimmung von Intersektionalität und in der Aufzählung der MIRA-Metriken, keine Passage macht ein Ergebnis von einer Achsenkombination abhängig, daher kein Intersectional. Schadensart Exclusionary_Norms aus dem eigenen Prüfkriterium zu binären Kategorien, die strukturelle Diskriminierung und das maskulinistische Intelligenzverständnis sind zitiert. Maßnahmen: Prüfung von Trainingsdaten auf Diversität und synthetische Trainingsdaten bei MIRA (Pre_Processing), diverse Teams, Stakeholder-Beteiligung, Feminist Design Tool, Gesetzgebung und Wartungszyklen (Organisational_Process). Demonstrated bezieht sich allein auf MIRA als umgesetztes und vorgestelltes Beispiel ohne berichtete Evaluation, die übrigen Maßnahmen bleiben Vorschläge. Other_Task: medizinische Diagnostik im MIRA-Praxisbeispiel. Handlungsfeld bleibt Not_SW_Specific, weil das Werk KI allgemein adressiert und Gesundheit nur das Feld eines Beispiels ist. Social_Construct aus der Bestimmung des Patriarchats als Machtsystem, in dem Männer Macht halten. Die Kritik binärer Geschlechterkategorien ist ein Gestaltungsprinzip ohne nicht-binäre Analysekategorie, daher kein Non_Binary_Inclusive. Gender wird nicht in einem eigenen Satz bestimmt. Bias-Verständnis nur implizit über systemische Machtstrukturen als Ursache von Ungleichheit. Das MIRA-Beispiel beruht nach eigener Angabe auf einem Interview mit dem Start-up.

analysis.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the over-representation of families from certain ethnic backgrounds in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers, Turner et al. 2020, absent from the reference list) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only as single-sentence cited cases in 4.1.1, and gender only in the enumeration 'racial, gender, or socio-economic disparities', so they stay uncoded. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the review's own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data that affect access to services and child welfare interventions, an allocation through biased data rather than the attribute itself; the work does not classify the discrimination. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing); auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process); none is assessed. AN_Task: predictive risk assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support), mental-health chatbots (Counselling_Client_Communication), NLP summaries of case notes and automated documentation (Documentation_Recording), AI tools and AI-driven personalised learning in social work education and training (Teaching_Further_Education, Sections 5.3.3 and 6.1.1). Source quality: several in-text citations do not match the reference list, for example 'Baker et al., 2021' cited for NLP documentation while reference [3] is a review of AI in net-zero building design, 'Chukwunweike et al.' cited for predictive analytics in social work while reference [9] concerns loop execution in deep-learning systems, and 'Turner et al., 2020' absent from the list; this limits the evidential weight of the cited case studies without changing the publication type.

analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.

analysis.AN_Notes: Prompts des GenderPair-Benchmarks (Instruktion, Pair Set, Requirement) dienen als Messinstrument, Robustheit wird über drei Promptstrukturen geprüft, keine Prompting-Technik im Sinne des Codebuchs. Bias-Achse Geschlecht über drei Gruppen, transgender und nicht-binäre Identitäten bilden Gruppe 3. Das Werk führt alle drei Gruppen als Geschlechtsidentitäten und bestimmt Gender Bias über die Geschlechtsidentität, daher nur Gender und nicht zusätzlich Sexual_Orientation_Identity. Die Einbeziehung nicht-binärer Gruppen steht in AN_Gender_Understanding als Non_Binary_Inclusive. Race, Alter, Nationalität und Religion erscheinen nur im Ausblick (Abschnitt 6). Schadensarten: Stereotypisierung über Bias-Pair Ratio sowie Winoqueer und StereoSet, Toxizität als eigene Metrik je Gruppe. Regard-Differenzen messen Stimmung und begründen nach Regel 1.4.1 keine Disparate_Performance. Erasure nicht-binärer Personen wird nur aus Ovalle et al. zitiert. Maßnahmen: Counterfactual Data Augmentation zum Debiasing-Datensatz (Pre_Processing) und LoRA-Fine-Tuning (In_Training), in eigenen Experimenten evaluiert mit Bias-Reduktion auf GenderPair, Winoqueer, BOLD und StereoSet und Leistungsprüfung auf GLUE und MMLU. AN_Task None, allgemeiner LLM-Benchmark ohne Anwendungsaufgabe. analysis.AN_Notes: Kritischer Review von 30 AI-Fairness-Papers entlang der sechs Intersektionalitäts-Tenets nach Collins und Bilge. Bias-Achsen: Race und Gender in ihrer Verschränkung als eigenes Argument (Black women als Beispiel intersektionaler Subgruppen, Kritik an der two-by-two analysis of gender by race). Schadensarten aus dem eigenen Argument über die Fairness-Forschung selbst: Erasure der Marginalisierten durch rein technische Fairness-Praxis und westlicher Default-Kontext (Exclusionary_Norms). AN_Mitigation_Stage codiert das Pipeline-Inventar (pre-, in-, post-processing), das die Synthese als Tagging-Kategorie strukturiert, sowie die eigenen organisatorischen Empfehlungen (Reflexivität, Zitierintegrität, Community-Einbindung, Anreize der Leitung); der Review bewertet Engagement mit Intersektionalität, nicht die Wirksamkeit der Interventionen, daher Proposed. AN_Gender_Definition Explicit über die als Bewertungsgrundlage übernommene Bestimmung nach Collins und Bilge, dass Macht soziale Teilungen wie gender hervorbringt (3 Intersectionality overview, Social Power); dieselbe Stelle trägt Social_Construct. Eine eigenständige Definition von gender gibt das Werk nicht.

Intersectional nicht codiert: gemessen wird das gemeinsame Vorkommen zweier Themen im Diskurs, kein Ergebnis, das von der Kombination der Achsen abhängt; die Deutung über Collins matrix of domination steht im Theoriebezug. AN_Harm_Types None: Schadensmechanismen (maskuline Technikkultur, stereotype Assistenten, Gesichtserkennung, Recruiting) stehen nur im zitierten Theorieteil, das eigene Ergebnis betrifft Diskurs und Nutzerinnenverhalten. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only und AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical folgen der Analyse, die Nutzer:innen binär über gender-guesser und she/her- oder he/him-Angaben klassifiziert; die einmalige Wendung gender as a narrow social construct in der Gliederungspassage der Einleitung (1. Introduction) bestimmt Geschlecht nicht und wird von der Analyse nicht eingelöst. Maßnahmen nur empfohlen: Parität in Entwicklungsteams, Rechtsrahmen, Förderung von Frauen in STEM und KI-Gründungen (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Task None: NLP ist Forschungsmethode des Werks, keine vorgeschlagene Praxisaufgabe.

Language_Culture covers cultural context and Global North hegemony in depictions of food and settings; Physical_Appearance covers body size and conventional attractiveness. Mitigation proposals: better curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), and algorithmic reparation, regulation, criminal culpability and diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all proposed. Studientyp Empirisch rather than Experimentell because the prompt contrasts serve an interpretative analysis without a controlled comparison. The confederate flag is discussed as violent imagery, but Toxicity is not coded because the codebook ties it to language. AN_Task None because the work audits a general image generator without a professional application task. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only: the passages after Guillaumin and on intersectionality determine power systems and the interplay of oppressions, not bias or discrimination, and the work sets 'biases' in quotation marks without determining it. Fairness teilweise rests on the recommendations structured around algorithmic reparation as a foundation for building, evaluating and adjusting machine learning systems, with deliberate intervention and training data curation, a subordinate treatment of fair system design.

analysis.AN_Notes: Drei präregistrierte Experimente zur Wirkung KI-generierter Vorurteile auf Vertrauenswürdigkeit und Nutzungsabsicht. Die ChatGPT-Antworten mit Gehaltsdisparitäten sind von den Autor:innen konstruierte Stimuli, das Werk misst nicht, ob LLMs solche Ausgaben erzeugen. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination codiert die im Stimulus gezeigte Gehaltszuteilung, die über stereotyp Schwarze oder weibliche Vornamen (Jerome, Judi) variiert, nach der Regel zu namensbasierten Variationen. Grenzfall, weil der Mechanismus Gegenstand des eigenen Arguments ist, aber nicht am Modell gemessen wird. AN_Prompting_Role None, der gezeigte Prompt ist Teil des Stimulus und ruft kein Modellverhalten hervor. Minderung nur vorgeschlagen in 5.5, Nachjustieren der auf verzerrten Daten trainierten Algorithmen (In_Training) und Schulungen durch Lehrende oder Organisationen (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird binär verglichen, Personen anderen Geschlechts fallen aus den paarweisen Korrelationen heraus, der Satz zu Geschlechterrollen statt biologischem Geschlecht steht im Forschungsstand und trägt die Analyse nicht. analysis.AN_Notes: Normatives Rahmenwerk aus Werten, Prinzipien und elf Politikfeldern für Mitgliedstaaten. Bias-Achsen: Geschlecht als eigenes Politikfeld (Policy Area 6, Ziffern 87 bis 93), Sprache und Kultur über die Wirkung von NLP-Anwendungen auf gefährdete Sprachen, Dialekte und tonale Variationen (Policy Area 7, Ziffer 95). Die langen Listen geschützter Merkmale sind Aufzählungen und bleiben uncodiert. Armutslücke (Ziffer 51), Stadt-Land-Gefälle (Ziffern 28, 67) und LMICs behandeln Zugangsungleichheit und digitale Spaltung, nicht Bias eines Systems entlang einer Achse, daher weder Socioeconomic noch Other_Axis. Schadensarten: Stereotypisierung aus dem eigenen Argument zur Reproduktion von Bias und Stereotypen (Ziffern 2(c), 66 und 90), Erasure aus dem Verschwinden gefährdeter Sprachen und Dialekte durch NLP-Anwendungen (Ziffer 95). Diskriminierende algorithmische Entscheidungen (Ziffer 29) werden ohne Zuteilungsfall und ohne Einordnung als unmittelbar oder mittelbar genannt und daher nicht codiert. Maßnahmen: Datenvorbereitung (diverse Trainingsdaten, Gold-Standard-Datensätze, nach Geschlecht disaggregierte Annotation, Ziffern 67 und 76) und Organisation (Ethical Impact Assessment mit Gender-Perspektive, AI Ethics Officers, Aufsicht, Audit, Zertifizierung, diverse Teams), durchgehend als Empfehlung, daher Proposed. AN_Task None: das Instrument regelt die Governance von KI über alle Sektoren und nennt Einsatzfelder wie Gesundheit oder Kulturerbe nur allgemein, ohne eine bestimmte berufliche Aufgabe. Geschlecht erscheint als Mädchen und Frauen gegenüber Männern ohne eigene Bestimmung, strukturelle Gender-Gaps (Ziffer 89) werden benannt, eine ausdrückliche Aussage zu Geschlecht als sozialer Konstruktion fehlt. Bias-Verständnis implizit über Nicht-Diskriminierung im Menschenrechtsrahmen, Ziffer 28 bestimmt Fairness als inklusiven Zugang zu den Vorteilen von KI. Kein Theoriebezug, das Völkerrecht ist ein rechtlich-normativer Bezug. Soziale_Arbeit nein, welfare erscheint nur in einer Aufzählung menschenrechtssensibler Einsatzbereiche (Ziffer 62).

analysis.AN_Notes: Bias measurement framework (LIBRA, EiCAT metric) for local cultural contexts, applied to New Zealand, a youth corpus and Malaysian English. Language_Culture is the axis the work analyses (local culture, Te Reo Maori and Malay words). The dataset spans eight target groups (age, gender, race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, physical appearance, disability, nationality, religion), but results are reported only in aggregate per model and context, so these axes are not coded and gender is not an object of the analysis. Stereotyping: the measured preference for stereotyped over anti-stereotyped sentences. Disparate_Performance: models fail to understand local non-English words, a quality difference between language varieties. Prompting appears only as a template for definition extraction. Bias is determined explicitly through the adopted definition of [14] and the JSD-based measure. No mitigation is applied or specified: the concluding sentence on 'incorporating localized and contextually rich data in evaluating and improving LLM fairness' and the remark on continuous improvements in model training are generic and name no identifiable intervention, so no stage is coded.

analysis.AN_Notes: Thematic analysis of 63 FAccT and AIES papers, evaluated in a workshop with AI experts. The workshop gauged perceived actionability of intermediate recommendation versions, not the effect of an applied mitigation, so the status stays Proposed. Gender is treated only within the intersectional frame and is not defined; race, not gender, is explicitly called a social construct, so Social_Construct is not coded. The paper reports its own regression on AI hiring scores with gender as a binary dummy predictor (Direct_Discrimination) and an ANOVA of facial-recognition error rates by gender and race (Disparate_Performance), where Black women show error rates that differ from both White women and Black men (Intersectional). Nonbinary individuals are named only as stakeholders for participatory design, so the analysis stays Binary_Categorical; no explicit statement that gender is socially produced. Mitigation (inclusive datasets, bias audits, participatory design, diverse teams, policy) is recommended only; the survey measures perceptions, not an intervention. Source-quality flag for domain experts: the provenance of the hiring data, the facial-recognition datasets and the survey sample is not documented, the facial-recognition figures follow the cited Gender Shades pattern, and Table 4 reports frequencies summing to 130 with percentages computed on 125 and 10 respondents as 4 percent. The empirical study type and both harm types rest on these reported results.

analysis.AN_Notes: Dataset and stereotype examination of GPT-3 and ChatGPT across intersectional groups built from six demographic categories. Other_Axis: political leaning (conservative and progressive) is one of the six categories from which the analysed groups are constructed and enters the measured results, for example 'conservative Muslim men'; political opinion is a recognised ground of discrimination, so it is coded as a further social axis. Role_Persona: simulated life-story roles the models answer as; Self_Criticism: ChatGPT filters stereotypes in its own generated responses. Gender is introduced in section 2.1 as men and women, but Table 1 and Tables C1 and C2 include non-binary groups as categories of the analysis, so Non_Binary_Inclusive follows the analysis (internal inconsistency of the source). Bias is determined explicitly as consistent answers in one category across trials (Stereotype Degree). Mitigation: the limitations recommend that future work 'cautiously regulate the output through effective prompting' to counter biases that the LLM's viewpoints introduce into the dataset, a proposed prompt-level measure; the general call for future de-biasing names no stage. Intersectionality is used as a combination of demographic attributes without a named theory, so no theory reference is coded.

analysis.AN_Notes: Feministische Policy-Analyse von sieben internationalen AI-Safety-Initiativen mit einem eigenen Bewertungsraster (vier Ziele mit je drei Fragen, Punktwerte je Initiative). Die Achsen stammen aus dem eigenen Argument gegen eine vermeintlich universelle Bedrohung im Befund zu combat neutrality, nämlich eine einkommensschwache Familie, die durch einen diskriminierenden Algorithmus Sozialleistungen verliert (Socioeconomic), sowie ländliche und indigene Gemeinschaften ohne Wasserzugang durch Rechenzentren (Race_Ethnicity für indigen, Other_Axis für den Wohnort im ländlichen Raum). Geschlecht steht nur in Aufzählungen, im Intersektionalitätsbegriff und im zitierten UN-Text, daher keine Gender-Achse. Intersektionalität ist Rahmen und Bewertungsziel, ein Ergebnis, das von einer Achsenkombination abhängt, fehlt, daher weder Intersectional in AN_Bias_Axes noch in AN_Gender_Understanding. Exclusionary_Norms folgt aus dem eigenen Befund, dass die Initiativen eine universelle, neutrale Sicht auf Risiko setzen und Erfahrungen marginalisierter Gruppen auslassen. Das Wohlfahrtsbeispiel ist eine allokative Benachteiligung, die das Werk weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung einordnet, und bleibt ohne Diskriminierungscode. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind Audits mit dem Framework, Rechenschaftspflicht von Unternehmen, Beteiligung marginalisierter Gruppen, Bürger:innenjurys und digitale Literacy (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird nicht bestimmt, und das Werk sagt nicht selbst, dass Geschlecht sozial hergestellt oder eine Machtstruktur ist. Die Wendung 'gendered systems of oppression' beschreibt den Zweck des übernommenen Rahmens nach McPhail, daher nach der Schwelle von 1.4.1 kein Social_Construct, sondern Unclear mit Absent. Bias wird als Reproduktion sozialer Ungleichheit und Machtverhältnisse gerahmt, aber nicht bestimmt, die Crenshaw-Passage bestimmt Intersektionalität und nicht Bias. Theorien sind Intersektionalität nach Crenshaw, das Feminist Policy Analysis Framework nach McPhail und Data Feminism nach D'Ignazio und Klein.

analysis.AN_Notes: Higher-education framework of the Open University for staff and students under an EDIA lens. General_Guidance strategies, verbatim: 'engage in equitable and inclusive prompting when required', 'Use the same/different prompt(s) several times with the same/different tool(s) and compare the outputs to identify and mitigate potential (cultural) bias.', 'Engage in a conversation with AI to challenge detected biases.' and 'prompting for inclusivity'. The comparison of outputs serves bias detection and is not combined into one answer, so Ensembling is not coded. Bias axes appear only in an enumeration (gender, cultural, disability, racial), so no axis is coded. Epistemic injustice and the non-inclusive nature of outputs are asserted as premises without a mechanism the framework itself develops, so no harm type is coded. Mitigation: inclusive prompting practice and embedding Critical AI Literacy in curricula and staff development, proposed. Critical Digital Literacy and epistemic injustice frame the treatment of bias.
