analysis.AN_Notes: Policy report on data quality, business models and alternatives for foundation models, addressed in the preface to practitioners and decision-makers of mission-driven organisations including social services and migration counselling. AN_Population General_Social_Work with the caveat that the addressees also include environmental and other common-good organisations. AN_Task Counselling_Client_Communication from chatbots in migration counselling, social benefit advice and crisis hotlines. Bias axes: Language_Culture (American English and majority-culture dominance, low-resource languages) and Socioeconomic (digital divide by design, only the wealthy benefit fully). Gender appears in cited examples (Bolukbasi et al. on 'professor', Wikipedia editors, the Austrian employment-agency chatbot), a pronoun ambiguity remark and the preface only and is not coded as an axis. Physical_Appearance from the report's own uncited worked example of the 'dumb' and 'blonde' association in section 3.3.1. Harm types from the report's own argument: erasure of smaller languages and regional variation, American English as stand-in for global knowledge (Exclusionary_Norms), propagation of majority stereotypes. Disparate_Performance and discrimination are named only through cited cases. Mitigation: deliberate curation and multilingual sources (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning, RLHF and constitutional AI as described alternatives (In_Training), transparency, external evaluation, participation and monitoring by organisations (Organisational_Process), all as recommendations. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit from the report's own determination of bias as partiality toward some groups, ideas or practices, framed as culturally variable. AN_Theory_Reference No: monoculture (Scott 1998), the 3Cs framework and data sovereignty frame data curation and compensation, not the treatment of gender or bias. Studientyp Empirisch from the stated method with expert interviews and comparative system analysis, the report is largely conceptual. AI Agent Review: KI_Sonstige teilweise from the report's own argument on the machine-learning dataset lineage (ImageNet, WordNet) of foundation models and the appendix on ML infrastructures, not from the cited child-protection case. Feministisch nein because 'patriarchal' appears once in the publisher's preface and is not developed. Misrepresentation from the expert-interview finding that regional cultures are decontextualized by outside voices, with the sutra example. AN_Population General_Social_Work follows the explicit addressing of social services in the preface, which the domain experts should confirm, since the main text addresses mission-driven organisations in general.

analysis.AN_Notes: Systematic review of nine implementation studies of predictive risk tools in child welfare, structured by CFIR and the ethical evaluation frameworks of Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020). AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated is a synthesised evaluation, not the review's own experiment: the review reports that the post-processing fairness correction of Purdy and Glass (2023), group-specific risk thresholds, reduced false positive and false negative error rates among four subgroups; it also reports the racial equity report of Putnam-Hornstein et al. (2022) finding comparable accuracy across racial and ethnic groups. Other mitigation stages remain description or recommendation: exclusion of bias-prone variables after community consultation and feature selection (Pre_Processing), stakeholder consensus, training against automation bias and external ethics reviews (Organisational_Process). Race_Ethnicity is the axis of the synthesised subgroup analyses, thresholds and equity reports; gender is mentioned once as a subgroup dimension of accuracy checks and socioeconomic status only in a cited discussion sentence, so both stay uncoded. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis: subgroup error rates and equity in subgroups as Disparate_Performance, historical bias in administrative records and racial disparities in screening outcomes as Indirect_Discrimination. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted equity criterion of Russell (2015), 'equity evaluates whether predictions function consistently across subgroups'. AN_Theory_Reference No (resolved by the AI Agent Review): Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020) are evaluation criteria and a practical framework that the review uses as an assessment checklist, and CFIR is an implementation framework; the review itself names the limited use of theoretical frameworks as a gap and mentions feminist and other critical theories only as a future-research suggestion. Boundary case flagged for domain experts.

analysis.AN_Notes: Experiment with Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 3 (via ChatGPT-4) and Adobe Firefly on 16 base prompts with demographic modifiers and modifier order. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'combining base prompts with modifiers and their sequencing', 'Base Prompt + Modifier' versus 'Modifier + Base'. Prompts are the measurement instrument and prompt modification is itself analysed and found insufficient as bias control. Bias axes as named by the work: gender, race, geography (coded Nationality_Migration, e.g. Korean soldier, US politician, person in Africa) and region/culture (coded Language_Culture, e.g. Lunar New Year); religion appears only as category label for pastor and monk prompts that are evaluated for gender and race, so Religion is not coded. Combined prompts such as 'Monk who is black' are not analysed for interaction effects, so Intersectional is not coded. Mitigation evaluated with a mixed result (modifiers shift distributions but not consistently, order matters). Gender is counted male/female in the result tables. analysis.AN_Notes: Prompt experiment with ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot on four policy scenarios (restrooms, snow removal, office temperature, business-trip expenses), each prompt variant submitted 50 times in neutral, male, female and partly non-binary or new-mother versions; themes retained at a 70 percent threshold. Prompting is the research instrument and the object of the central finding. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'the importance of precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications', i.e. naming the gendered target group explicitly in the prompt; the work adds that equity principles must be embedded 'not just in prompts'. Other_Task: drafting workplace and municipal policy recommendations, outside social work. Bias_Axes: gender is varied in every scenario, and non-binary employees are an analysed group of their own (restroom and business-trip prompts), coded as Sexual_Orientation_Identity under the codebook label for gender identity; race, class and ability appear only as intersecting factors in the discussion, so Intersectional is not coded. Harm types from the work's own results: male default (Exclusionary_Norms), omission of women's and non-binary needs in unspecified prompts (Erasure), baby-changing facilities only in women's restrooms read as care stereotype (Stereotyping). Mitigation only proposed: curated gender-balanced and intersectional datasets (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning (In_Training), equity principles in prompts (Prompt_Practice), audits, Human-in-the-Loop oversight and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Social_Construct rests on the applied statement after Connell that gender relations are institutionally embedded in everyday practices; the work also uses metabolic differences between women and men as a factual premise. Theory frame: Tronto's ethics of care, Young's justice as inclusion, capabilities approach, Connell, Grosz, feminist spatial planning, design justice.

Generative_KI is teilweise: the work frames its object as large language models and language generation, but its method and experiments concern encoder-only masked language models. Prompting is the proposed mitigation practice; soft prompt tuning belongs to none of the technique families, and in-context learning appears only as motivation, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing; the trained parameters are prompt embeddings, not the model, so In_Training is not coded. The intervention changes the model input, coded Prompt_Practice. Evaluated with mixed results (on par with the state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. Harm type: stereotyping measured by the StereoSet stereotype score; the Gallegos harm list in the introduction is background and not coded. Gender is operationalised as he/she and male/female name pairs without a definition. Bias is determined technically by the stereotype score near 50 percent and by the reference distribution averaged across groups. AN_Task None: benchmark study without an application task.

Generative_KI is teilweise: the work frames its object as large language models and language generation, but its method and experiments concern encoder-only masked language models. Prompting is the proposed mitigation practice; soft prompt tuning belongs to none of the technique families, and in-context learning appears only as motivation, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing; the trained parameters are prompt embeddings, not the model, so In_Training is not coded. The intervention changes the model input, coded Prompt_Practice. Evaluated with mixed results (on par with the state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. Harm type: stereotyping measured by the StereoSet stereotype score; the Gallegos harm list in the introduction is background and not coded. Gender is operationalised as he/she and male/female name pairs without a definition. Bias is determined technically by the stereotype score near 50 percent and by the reference distribution averaged across groups. AN_Task None: benchmark study without an application task.

The antiracist research framework (Goings et al. 2023) frames the treatment of bias.

AN_Harm_Types Stereotyping über die Korrelation mit pro- und antistereotypen Sets, Exclusionary_Norms über überwiegend männliche Formen ohne Genderhinweis, Disparate_Performance über die Differenz der Erkennungsgüte männlicher und weiblicher Terme (Delta G). analysis.AN_Notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). The work frames the problem as lack of diversity and unequal exposure rather than as bias; its understanding of bias is recognisable only from the entropy measures. Axes: nationality, ethnicity and region of generated names, cultural and language perspectives on social norms. Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). Gender appears only in a persona cue and a social-norm example.

analysis.AN_Notes: Edited volume (introduction, sixteen chapters, outlook) coded as one Work; codes collect what individual chapters carry as their own argument or result. Studientyp Theoretisch after the predominantly conceptual chapters; Plafky et al. report own usability tests and a focus group on an LLM case-note prototype, Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case, Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study. General_Guidance strategy: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, naechster Termin; Tabelle 1), and testers ask for selectable templates per note type; Botzum et al. propose mandatory documentation of the prompts students used. AN_Prompting_Role: Learning_Content from Beranek (prompting as communicative competence), Recommended_Practice from Plafky et al. and Botzum et al., Object_of_Critique from Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks as a manipulation practice. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender (Beranek's own example list, Schlomann's gendered digital divide), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner on the AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Disability (Steiner's chapter makes AI-related exclusion of disabled people its object and demands models that do not reinforce exclusion 'vor allem im Bereich Behinderung'), Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own argument), Socioeconomic (editors' Allegheny poverty example, Schlomann on education), Language_Culture (Plafky et al., own observation that Swiss German dialect recognition depends on proximity to Standard German), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case). Sexual orientation appears only in enumerations. Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without an own argument that depends on the combination. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating internet training data), Erasure (Steiner: data selection and weighting under-represent marginalised discourses and groups; Tappe: AI-generated visual narratives decide which cultural references remain invisible), Disparate_Performance (own observation on dialect recognition, a quality difference between language varieties). Amazon hiring, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, UNESCO images and Gender Shades are cited cases and stay uncoded under rule 1.4.1. AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process) are recommended; the AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns a decision-support tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation. AN_Gender_Definition Absent and AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender appears only in short discrimination examples, the cited gender gap of older women and men, and enumerations that also name LGBTQIA+ and queer people; no chapter determines gender, and these signals do not settle a binary or any other understanding. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit (Loehe; Dummann footnote 6; also Rottkemper). AN_Theory_Reference: Steiner frames under-representation and exclusion through a critical conception of inclusion and exclusion (Luhmann, Stichweh) with critical theory and Rojas' radical inclusion concept; Staub-Bernasconi, Media Equation and CASA frame ethics or communication, not gender or bias. Feministisch nein: no feminist theory or method and no structural gender critique.

analysis.AN_Notes: Other_Axis: marital or relationship status and household composition, analysed through the 'Really Single' model and the broad cohabitation definition. Gender is coded from the own survey with women's shelters on digital exclusion. Religion appears only as a co-mentioned proxy ground and is not coded. Intersectional is not coded, since intersectional discrimination is named in background and recommendations without a result that depends on a combination of axes. Harm types: Direct_Discrimination through citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs of the 'Model Abroad', Indirect_Discrimination through apparently neutral household, residency and income inputs acting as proxies and through digital-only access, Exclusionary_Norms through dominant-group norms of household and family embedded in the models and the digital-only default. Stereotyping of foreigners as fraud-prone is argued as a political narrative rather than a system output and is left uncoded. No group-level quality difference could be measured because demographic data was denied, so Disparate_Performance is not coded. Mitigation: proposed ban on citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs (Pre_Processing) and proposed caseworker training, impact assessments, audits, transparency, independent oversight and non-digital access (Organisational_Process). UDK's equalisation of true positive rates is reported and criticised, not presented as an evaluated mitigation. analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

analysis.AN_Notes: Interviewstudie (25 Teilnehmende) mit vorab erzeugten ChatGPT-Antworten auf vier Prompts, in denen person durch man, woman, non-binary person ersetzt wird. Prompts dienen als Forschungsinstrument und als vorgeschlagene Test-Suite; die Ersetzung des Personenbegriffs ist keine Technik der Prompt-Report-Familien, daher AN_Prompt_Techniques None. Sexual_Orientation_Identity codiert, weil nicht-binäre und trans Personen als eigene Analysegruppe geführt werden (Geschlechtsidentität); das Werk nennt die Achse gender, daher beide Werte. Schadensarten aus der eigenen Output-Analyse (3.1) und den Interviewbefunden (4.6.2): Stereotyping, cis-zentrischer Default (Exclusionary_Norms), Reduktion nicht-binärer Figuren auf Identitätskämpfe (Misrepresentation). Tonunterschiede nicht als Disparate_Performance codiert (Codebuch 1.4.1), wahrgenommene Genauigkeit gleich über Gruppen. Maßnahmen nur vorgeschlagen: diversere Trainingsdaten und Co-Design bei der Datenkuratierung (Pre_Processing), Rückfragen des Modells bei vagen Prompts (Intra_Processing, 5.2.2), Co-Design, Prompt-Test-Suite und Echtzeit- sowie Community-Bias-Auditing (Organisational_Process). Grounded Theory und reflexive thematische Analyse sind Methoden, keine Theorie, die Gender oder Bias rahmt.

analysis.AN_Notes: UNESCO reference framework of twelve AI competency blocks for school students (four aspects by three progression levels) with curricular goals, pedagogical methods, learning environments and assessment items. Inclusivity is one of five key principles with its own section (2.4), hence Diversitaet ja. Bias enters as the non-discrimination principle, as anti-bias measures within section 2.4, the data biases lab and the competency to critique AI-amplified biases; it recurs as learning content beside privacy, human agency and environmental sustainability and is not the framework's central contribution, hence Bias_Ungleichheit teilweise. AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, ethnicity, culture, ability, socio-economic status and language appear only in enumerations of bias types or disaggregation variables. AN_Harm_Types None: no harm mechanism is established for the framework's own object. AN_Mitigation_Stage: Pre_Processing (representative data, data engineering to remove identifiable biases in the data biases lab), In_Training (anti-discrimination and discrimination-free training methods), Organisational_Process (public validation before recommending AI tools, inclusive testing and auditing); all are recommended as curricular content or policy, hence Proposed. AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only. AN_Gender_Definition and AN_Gender_Understanding Not_Applicable: gender occurs only in enumerations. AN_Population Not_SW_Specific: school students in general education. AN_Task None: AI is the learning object of a school curriculum; students' own use of AI tools to practise writing is learning activity, not a task of professional practice, and AI-supported assessment by teachers appears only as a supplementary outlook in section 5.8. School teaching lies outside Teaching_Further_Education, which addresses professionals. AN_Prompting_Role None: prompts appear only in a privacy assessment item.

Disparate_Performance rests on the measured accuracy gap between masculine and feminine pronoun texts (Delta G) and the resolution bias in VLMs; Stereotyping on gender-stereotypical associations in reasoning. analysis.AN_Notes: Fallstudie der Organisation Queer in AI mit eigenen Mitglieder- und Empfängerbefragungen. Die in Abschnitt 2 gelisteten AI-Schäden (Outing, Hassrede, Zensur) sind zitiert; die eigene Analyse betrifft den Ausschluss queerer Menschen aus AI-Forschung, Konferenzen und Publikationswesen. Bias-Achsen, die die eigene Analyse der Teilhabebarrieren entwickelt: gender and sexual orientation (trans und nicht-binäre Personen als eigene Kategorien, Deadnaming), Einkommen (Bewerbungsgebühren, low-income scholars), Global South und Visa (Nationality_Migration), Behinderung und Neurodivergenz, Verstärkung bei intersecting identities. Race_Ethnicity erscheint nur in Demografie- und Reichweitenangaben, Kaste nur in einer Aufzählung (class or caste) und einem Paneltitel; beide bleiben uncodiert. Schadensarten aus eigenen Beobachtungen: exklusive Geschlechtsabfragen und Klarnamenzwang bei Konferenzregistrierung (Exclusionary_Norms), Chat-Software blockiert queere Begriffe (Erasure). Evaluated beschränkt sich auf die organisatorischen Maßnahmen der Organisation (Stipendienprogramm, Workshops, Konferenzleitfaden, Name-Check-Tool), deren Wirkung das Werk nach eigener Angabe bewertet (assess the organization's impact) und mit Befragungsergebnissen und Adoptionsstand berichtet, darunter das gemischte Ergebnis relatively modest adoption; es handelt sich um Maßnahmen gegen Ausschluss aus der AI-Forschung, nicht um technische Bias-Mitigation. Kein ausdrückliches Gender- oder Bias-Verständnis formuliert, Umfragekategorien führen nicht-binäre und weitere Geschlechter.

analysis.AN_Notes: Systematisches Review nach PRISMA. Achsen nach der eigenen Synthese, die Gender und Ethnizität als Faktoren der Fairness unterscheidet, Behinderung erscheint nur im Solidaritätsabschnitt neben anderen Gruppen und ist nicht codiert. Disparate_Performance: Gender- und Sampling-Bias mindern die Qualität klinischer Entscheidungsunterstützung für Frauen und ethnische Gruppen. Indirect_Discrimination nach der eigenen Benennung des Reviews, das US-Allokationsalgorithmus-Beispiel bleibt ohne Klassifikation direkt oder indirekt. Mitigation: Vorverarbeitung und diverse Datenerhebung (Pre_Processing), Stakeholder-Kooperation, Ethikkommissionen und Schulung (Organisational_Process), synthetisierte Vorschläge, deren Wirksamkeit die Autor:innen selbst als unbefriedigend einschätzen. Allgemeine Fairness-Constraints und Kompensation rechtfertigen keine weitere technische Stufe. Other_Task: klinische Diagnose und Entscheidungsunterstützung in der Gesundheitsversorgung. AN_Theory_Reference No: Jobin et al. und die EU-Leitlinien dienen als Kodierrahmen ethischer Prinzipien, nicht als Theorie von Gender oder Bias.

analysis.AN_Notes: Theoretische Erörterung von NLP in Beratung, Altenhilfe sowie Kinder- und Jugendhilfe. Bias wird nur in der Diskussion behandelt, ohne analysierte soziale Achse. Digitale Affinität ist keine soziale Achse im Sinne der Achsenregel, das Argument trägt aber Exclusionary_Norms (Ankerwerk MA3LBJS6 desselben Werks). Die Wiederholung stereotyper Rollenbilder ist nur aus Lucy und Bamman 2021 zitiert und bleibt als Schadensart unkodiert. Maßnahmen: interdisziplinäre Entwicklungsteams, Transparenz und nicht ausschließlich digitaler Erstkontakt, vorgeschlagen. Aufgaben: Chatbots im Erstkontakt und in der Beratung, Entscheidungsunterstützung (MAEWIN, Predictive Analytics) und Forschung (CASoTex, NLP-gestützte Inhaltsanalyse). Theoriebezug als Grenzfall: Staub-Bernasconis Konzept der Menschenrechtsprofession rahmt die Gesamtanalyse und wird in der Diskussion ausdrücklich auf das Diskriminierungsverbot bezogen. Bias-Verständnis nur implizit als Reproduktion vorhandener Kontexte.

analysis.AN_Notes: Reflective empirical account of the co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalised groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. Mitigation Demonstrated: the training within co-creation was applied and is reported only through facilitator and participant reflections, without a completed assessment of an effect on AI bias, although the work calls its approach an evaluation. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases, outside social work. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the training examples added by DAF (generative AI answers on fathers and mothers, gendered job endings in Google Translate, Section 5.1); Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for identity verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos, Section 4.1). Race_Ethnicity stays uncoded: postal codes as proxy of race appear only as a parenthetical example of a toolkit challenge (Section 4) and the participant consensus that white males benefit most from credit scoring is a single reported perception (Section 4.2); the enumeration 'gender, age, ethnic origin, and sexual orientation' and the participant groups are not coded either. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the gender-role examples demonstrated in the training, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the project's own toolkit is built to address. Gender is treated through examples only, without a stated or recognisable understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. AN_Theory_Reference Yes: critical and social-justice perspectives on participatory design (power relations, 'box-ticking', ethics-washing) frame the treatment of AI bias and training; boundary between framing tradition and methodological label. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organisations, but no social work practice is addressed. The Markdown conversion duplicates and scrambles parts of Sections 4.3 to 5.3; all quotes come from coherent passages.

Gemessene Black-white-Screen-in-Unterschiede (20 gegenüber 9 Prozentpunkten) tragen Bias, Fairness, Race_Ethnicity und Evaluated für diesen organisatorischen Entscheidungsprozess; §7.2 empfiehlt diversere Mitarbeitende als ergänzenden Aspekt. Das Analyseprofil ist quellengerecht. Die Interpretation bleibt eingeschränkt: §7.3 trennt geringere Disparität von nachgewiesener Gerechtigkeit und weist auf verschiedene Zeiträume der quantitativen und qualitativen Daten hin; keine pauschale Praxiswirksamkeit ableiten.
